thread.title: Hewlett-Packard (HPQ) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Hewlett-Packard (HPQ) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo Can Hewlett-Packard ( HPQ ) maintain its winning streak? And is it time for long-term value investors to seriously give the leading global PC manufacturer another chance?
The company is set to report second quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Tuesday. While the company has delivered sixth straight quarters of revenue growth, investors aren’t willing to forget the suffering they’ve been through due to multiple quarters of declines since 2010. On Tuesday, the company must demonstrate that the uptick in segments such as Personal Systems and Print, which improved last quarter, was no aberration.
For the quarter that ended April, the Palo Alto, Calif.-based company is expected to earn 48 cents per share on revenue on $13.57 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when the company earned 40 cents per share on $12.38 billion in revenue. For the full year, ending in October, earnings are projected to increase 20% year over year to $1.98 per share, while revenue of $56.56 billion would mark a 8.7% rise.
Since splitting from Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) in November 2015, HPQ — which retained the printing and PC portions of the business — has performed much better than Wall Street expected. And that’s been due to the strong leadership of President and CEO Dion Weisler, who has found a way to revive growth in the company’s Personal Systems and Print segments. As such, HP has begun 2018 on a strong note , delivering 14% surge in revenue, while profits have risen 26%.
The company’s decision to grow its capabilities in the high-end printer market has been wise move since that market also generate sales of high-margin accessories and supplies. Combined with improved marketing initiatives and pricing strategies, the company’s free cash flow profile has significantly improved, allowing the management to not only grow the dividend, but also buy back shares.
Nevertheless, the management on Tuesday must convince investors that HP can sustain its PC-shipment growth in an environment where hardware manufacturers — save for Apple ( AAPL ) — continue to struggle with profits. And given the gloomy state of the PC industry which has experienced fourteen straight quarters of declining global shipments, according to research firm Gartner, HP — given its status as the world’s largest PC manufacturer — is fighting an uphill battle.
All told, while HP appears to have righted the ship with its execution and improved free cash flow, the growth and popularity of mobile devices will continue to chip away at the PC business.And there isn’t enough growth in the printing segment (or margin) that would make these shares — despite their appealing valuation — a good investment today.
